chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who wakes up in the morning having not eaten, not drunk, and not made the intention for fasting, and he has one day of Ramadan upon him. Is it permissible for him to fast that day, given that most of the day has passed? He said, 'Yes, it is permissible for him to fast it and count it as one of the days of Ramadan.'
ai.seo_question: Does a person need to make the intention for fasting before dawn if they wake up without having eaten or drunk?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that the morning intention (niyyah) is not a strict condition for the validity of the Ramadan fast, provided one has not consumed food or drink. This ruling supports the Shia view of *niyyah* as a spiritual commitment rather than a rigid temporal prerequisite, allowing the fast to be valid even if the intention is made after sunrise, as long as the day is not already spent in consumption.
